body_long:
Two sommeliers from French palaces have won major titles in October 2026. Camille Guilbaud of Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc is a world champion of blind tasting, and Dimitri Nalin of Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's Paris has won the French edition of the Ruinart Sommelier Challenge. Both results were reported on 30 October.

## A world title in Avignon

The 14th World Blind Tasting Championship, organised by La Revue du vin de France, took place in Avignon on Saturday 17 October. More than 200 tasters from 41 nations took part. Each team had to identify twelve wines served without labels, giving the grape, the country, the appellation and the vintage, with about ten minutes per wine.

France was represented by Camille Guilbaud, 30, sommelier at Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc in Antibes, and Candy Sangare, founder of Art de Vivre by Candy. It was the first all-female French team. The pair finished first with 189 points, ahead of Japan on 181 and Brazil on 159. France was the only team to name the first wine, a 2010 Crémant de Luxembourg. The title was decided on the twelfth, a Sercial Madeira from Blandy's, which the Japanese team, then in the lead, took for a Boal.

It is France's fifth world title, after 2014, 2019, 2020 and 2025, and its second in a row. The duo had already won the French championship for 2025–2026.

## From veterinary studies to the Cap

Camille Guilbaud first studied to become a vet in Brazil, until Covid interrupted her studies. She then worked front of house in a French restaurant in São Paulo, where she met Candy Sangare. After her parents took over a wine estate north of Bordeaux, she trained in sommellerie through a work-study programme, then worked at the Lalique restaurant in Gironde and at La Dame de Pic, Anne-Sophie Pic's restaurant. She joined Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, part of Oetker Hotels, about three years ago. Its cellar holds more than 5,000 references. The hotel closed for the winter on 18 October and reopens on 18 April 2027.

## A Ruinart title for Fouquet's Paris

On 26 October, at Cheval Blanc Paris, Dimitri Nalin won the French edition of the Ruinart Sommelier Challenge 2026. He has been head sommelier at Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's Paris since July 2025. The day was devoted to rosé champagne, its ageing and its making. The jury included Caroline Fiot, cellar master of Maison Ruinart, sommelier Estelle Touzet, Alexis Goujard of La Revue du vin de France and Brice Beuzeville-Loiseau, the 2025 winner. Amandine Sahuquet of 67 Pall Mall in Bordeaux finished second, and Nathanaël Piètre of Maison Despouès third.

## The signal

In the palaces, the wine team has become part of the reason to book. A titled sommelier gives a hotel a story that guests, critics and future recruits all hear, and it keeps the house in the conversation even when, like the Cap, it is closed for the season.
summary: Camille Guilbaud of Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc won the 14th World Blind Tasting Championship for France with Candy Sangare (189 points, Avignon, 17 October). Dimitri Nalin, head sommelier at Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's Paris, won the French Ruinart Sommelier Challenge 2026 at Cheval Blanc Paris on 26 October. Both reported on 30 October.
title: Palace sommeliers take two titles: Cap-Eden-Roc world champion, Fouquet's Paris wins Ruinart
